District Monitoring Officer and Employment and Training Director C. Palani inspecting the monsoon precautionary works in Madurai on Sunday. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT
In response to the ongoing Northeast monsoon rainfall, officials convened a review meeting here on Sunday to evaluate extensive precautionary and safety measures across the district.
Led by District Monitoring Officer and Employment and Training Director C. Palani—alongside District Collector Nishanth Krishna and Madurai Corporation Commissioner Gaurav Kumar—the gathering brought together representatives from a wide array of municipal, administrative, infrastructure, and emergency services departments.
Reviewing the current weather forecasts predicting heavy rainfall, Mr. Palani instructed departments to operate in complete coordination to safeguard the public.
Key directives included the immediate deployment of motor pumps to clear waterlogging in low-lying areas and ensuring that temporary relief camps are fully equipped to provide uninterrupted basic necessities, such as quality food, purified drinking water, and medical care, to displaced residents.
Authorities highlighted that an emergency control room remains operational around the clock at the District Collectorate, with citizens instructed to dial the toll-free helpline 1077 for rain-related emergencies and grievances.
Continuous surveillance is currently underway across 27 identified vulnerable low-lying zones, comprising 17 urban areas within the corporation limits and 10 rural pockets, said a press statement.
Temporary relief shelters—including schools, colleges, and marriage halls—have been fully prepared.
Further, heavy-duty pumps, super-sucker vehicles, earthmovers, power saws, and adequate stockpiles of sandbags for river and tank bund reinforcement have been positioned strategically across the district.
Water resource officials are also closely tracking inflow, storage, and discharge levels at major reservoirs such as Periyar and Vaigai, the statement added.
Following the meeting, Mr. Palani, accompanied by the District Collector and the Corporation Commissioner, carried out a field inspection of critical infrastructure points in the city.
The team visited the Vaigai-Yanaikkal low-level bridge to verify that rainwater flows unobstructed, directing field personnel to promptly clear accumulated plastic waste, tree branches, and debris from beneath the structure.
At the Sellur Pandalkudi canal, officials reviewed drainage flow paths and bank stability to prevent overflows from infiltrating adjacent residential neighbourhoods.
The team inspected the low-lying areas surrounding the Madurai Periyar Bus Stand and the railway station—major transit hubs witnessing heavy passenger footfall.
Engineers were instructed to keep high-power dewatering pumps operational to prevent water stagnation and ensure pedestrian and traffic safety remain uncompromised.
